title: CLAUDE.md
text: localalloc — R package implementing ten facility-location optimization models (LSCP, MCLP, P-Median, P-Center, UFCLP, CFLP, DP, UFLP, MAXCAP, PMAXCAP) integer linear programs, built sparse matrices solved directly via Rglpk highs (default). Author: Philippe Apparicio (USherbrooke). ten exported; result objects carry class localalloc_result. repo root package root (DESCRIPTION, NAMESPACE, R/, man/, tests/ top level). data-raw/ holds scripts generated data/*.rda (import-legacy-data.R real bixi_* case study, sample-data.R small sample_* fixtures).

title: CLAUDE.md
text: Ten model functions (R/lscp.R, mclp.R, p_center.R, p_median.R, ufclp.R, cflp.R, dp.R, uflp.R, maxcap.R, pmaxcap.R), one shared internal helper file R/utils.R (validation, matrix building, result extraction, English-language stop()/warning() messages), plus R/print.R (print.localalloc_result) R/visualize.R (plot_sites() — interactive mapview map candidate/demand/existing sf layers; mapview Suggests, guarded requireNamespace()). ten models follow shape: validate inputs → build cost matrix via od_to_matrix() → derive valid <- (.finite(cost_mat), arr.ind = TRUE) (-cutoff/-radius pairs get decision variable , keeping MIP sparse) → build objective/constraints directly Matrix::sparseMatrix() (never dense matrix, never symbolic DSL) → dispatch solve_direct(L, , dir, rhs, types, lower, upper, sense, solver) utils.R → extract solution → return structure(list(...), class = "localalloc_result"). Check actual function/NAMESPACE assuming helper name — file drifted code . Solver engine — ompr/ROI. Earlier versions built MIP ompr::MIPModel() solved via ompr.roi::with_ROI(). dropped: ompr’s objective-vector construction (objective_function.linear_optimization_model) assigns coefficients Matrix::sparseVector one element time, assignment re-sorts whole structure — cheap individually, catastrophic aggregate problems tens thousands terms (minutes, regardless solver ompr asked use). solve_direct() bypasses entirely: model builds sparse /L/dir/rhs/types , solve_direct() hands straight Rglpk::Rglpk_solve_LP() (solver "glpk") highs::highs_solve() ("highs", default — genuinely faster glpk now ompr bottleneck gone, confirmed bixi_* case study). types = "B" works natively glpk; highs ’s translated "" + bounds [0,1] (highs package binary type). Variable order within model’s vector whatever model’s comment block documents (typically [Y, X] [Y, X, Z]) — read top sparse-matrix block touching indices. existing_sites (LSCP/MCLP/P-Median/P-Center/UFLP) “Required Facilities”: forced open via X_j == 1 constraint row. p_facilities models (MCLP/P-Median/P-Center/UFLP) count inside budget — budget row sum(X) == p spans candidates existing sites, p_facilities total number open facilities p_facilities - n_exist candidates get selected. Validation therefore requires n_exist <= p_facilities <= n_fac + n_exist. MAXCAP/PMAXCAP exception: existing_sites competitor sites, , p_facilities still bounds candidates . five Required-Facilities models return every open facility sf_selected — selected candidates forced-open existing_sites — via bind_selected_sites(), source column ("candidate" / "existing") distinguishing . n_open == nrow(sf_selected). MAXCAP / PMAXCAP return candidates (existing_sites competitor’s). Key shared helpers utils.R (internal, roxygen @export): - validate_sf() / validate_cost_matrix() — input validation, English stop()/warning() messages. - od_to_matrix() — long OD data.frame → wide matrix, Inf missing/-cutoff pairs. - replace_inf() — swaps Inf large finite value; still used dp() (missing-pair fallback, cutoff concept ) maxcap()/pmaxcap() (comparison sentinel competitor-baseline bij matrix) — used assignment-style models anymore, since now create decision variable pairs already finite. - make_coverage_matrix() — distance matrix → binary coverage matrix LSCP/MCLP. - set_weights() — fills missing weight columns sf objects 1. - extract_assignment() — turns data.frame(, j, value) solution back demand→facility assignment data.frame; solver-agnostic, unchanged ompr removal. - bind_selected_sites() — builds sf_selected output: selected candidates + forced-open existing_sites, reconciling id column name, id class, CRS, geometry column name, differing attribute sets (NA-filled), tagging row source. - solve_direct() — glpk/highs dispatcher described . Full test coverage exists — one test-<model>.R per model plus test-utils.R helper-fixtures.R. data/bixi_*.rda — real Sherbrooke Bixi case study (5,811 candidates × 176 demand pts × 25 existing stations; OD tables use from_id/to_id/ travel_time_p50 columns). 400-candidate subsample p_median() solves ~3s current (direct sparse-matrix) engine — previously 220s+ old ompr-based engine. Full-scale (5,811 candidates) re-benchmarked since rewrite; old OOM warning longer applies -(ompr-side dense variable blowup), re-test assuming ’s fine full scale. data/sample_*.rda — small fixtures quick manual runs.

title: Facility Location Optimization Models in R
text: Opens p_facilities facilities total maximize weighted demand covered within service_radius. Unlike LSCP, full coverage isn’t required – demand outside every open facility’s radius simply left uncovered. existing_sites, supplied, forced open count p_facilities, exactly P-Median. package also bundles real-world case study originates : 5,811 candidate sites, 176 demand points, 25 existing Bixi bike-share stations Sherbrooke, QC (see ?bixi-data full provenance data-licensing note). existing_sites treated Required Facilities – forced open, excluded automatically (warning) candidate two overlap, counted inside p_facilities. 25 existing stations, p_facilities = 35 opens 10 new ones. result’s sf_selected layer lists 35 open facilities, source column ("candidate" / "existing") telling apart. real ~5,800-variable MIP, toy example – solves 2 seconds default highs solver. 10 new stations plus 25 existing ones cover 67,050 74,200 total weighted demand (population + jobs) – 90%, opening 10 new sites within 15-minute walk.

text: Dispersion Problem takes demand layer – selects p_facilities candidate sites maximize minimum pairwise distance sites chosen, spreading much possible (e.g. siting facilities shouldn’t cluster together). title: Capacitated Fixed-charge Facility Location Problem (CFLP) — cflp
text: Extends ufclp() capacity limit per facility: total weighted demand assigned site exceed capacity. objective base constraints ufclp(), plus: $$\sum_{=1}^{n} a_i Y_{ij} \leq k_j X_j, \; \forall j$$ \(k_j\) = candidate_capacity.

title: Capacitated Fixed-charge Facility Location Problem (CFLP) — cflp
text: demand sf POINT. Demand points. demand_id character. Unique id column demand. demand_weight character NULL. Weight column demand. candidate sf POINT. Candidate facility sites. candidate_id character. Unique id column candidate. matrix_OD_candidates data.frame. Long OD table demand--candidate. matrix_OD_candidates_from_id character. matrix_OD_candidates_to_id character. matrix_OD_candidates_dist character. cutoff numeric NULL. Maximum impedance, expressed units OD table's distance column – may hold distance travel time. Pairs beyond dropped. NULL (default) means cutoff. candidate_fixed_cost character. Column candidate holding fixed cost opening site (f_j). candidate_capacity character. Column candidate holding site's maximum capacity (k_j). transport_cost_rate numeric. Cost per unit distance per unit demand (alpha). Default 1. solver character. "highs" (default) "glpk".

title: Dispersion Problem (DP) — dp
text: Selects p_facilities candidate sites maximize minimum pairwise distance opened sites (maximally spread-placement). Takes demand layer – pure site-dispersion problem among candidates. $$\text{Maximize } D$$ $$\text{s.t. } D \leq d_{ij} + (M - d_{ij})(1-X_i) + (M-d_{ij})(1-X_j), \; \forall ,j$$ $$\sum_{j} X_j = P \qquad X_j \\{0,1\}$$ \(D\) = min_distance output, \(P\) = p_facilities, \(M\) sufficiently large constant (computed internally 2 times maximum distance matrix).

title: Dispersion Problem (DP) — dp
code: dp(   candidate,   candidate_id,   matrix_OD_candidates,   matrix_OD_candidates_from_id = "from_id",   matrix_OD_candidates_to_id = "to_id",   matrix_OD_candidates_dist = "distance",   p_facilities,   solver = "highs" )

title: Dispersion Problem (DP) — dp
text: candidate sf POINT. Candidate sites. candidate_id character. Unique id column candidate. matrix_OD_candidates data.frame. Long candidate--candidate distance table (from_id/to_id/distance) – directions pair supplied. matrix_OD_candidates_from_id character. matrix_OD_candidates_to_id character. matrix_OD_candidates_dist character. p_facilities integer. Number sites select (>= 2). solver character. "highs" (default) "glpk".

title: Dispersion Problem (DP) — dp
text: object class localalloc_result.

title: Location Set Covering Problem (LSCP) — lscp
text: Finds minimum number facilities open every demand point covered least one facility within service_radius. $$\text{Minimize } z = \sum_{j=1}^{m} X_j$$ $$\text{s.t. } \sum_{j=1}^{m} b_{ij} X_j \geq 1, \; \forall \qquad X_j \\{0,1\}, \; \forall j$$ \(b_{ij} = 1\) site \(j\) covers demand \(\) (.e. \(d_{ij} \leq S\), \(S\) = service_radius), 0 otherwise.

title: Maximum Capture Problem (MAXCAP) — maxcap
text: Selects p_facilities candidate sites maximize weighted demand captured competitor (existing_sites), assuming demand point currently patronizes nearest existing site switches newly opened candidate closer. Reduced formulation: omits tie-breaking mechanism candidate incumbent competitor (assumes exact-distance ties). $$\text{Maximize } z = \sum_{\} w_i Y_i$$ $$\text{s.t. } Y_i \leq \sum_{j \p_i} X_j, \; \forall \qquad \sum_{j \J} X_j \leq P$$ $$X_j, Y_i \\{0,1\}$$ \(w_i\) = demand_weight, \(P\) = p_facilities, \(p_i\) set candidate sites closer \(\) nearest competitor.

title: Maximal Covering Location Problem (MCLP) — mclp

what: Maximum Capture Problem with Price (PMAXCAP) — pmaxcap
title: Maximum Capture Problem with Price (PMAXCAP) — pmaxcap
text: Extends maxcap() making firm's price decision variable. fixed set open sites, profit piecewise-linear price (capture flips threshold breakpoints), true global optimum found enumerating every breakpoint price, solving resulting MAXCAP-style linear MIP one, keeping best. needs nonlinear/MINLP solver. $$\text{Maximize } \Pi = (P^- v) \sum_{\} a_i Y_i^- \sum_{j \J} f_j X_j^$$ $$\text{s.t. } Y_i^\leq \sum_{j \N_i(b_i^B)} X_j^, \; \forall \qquad \sum_{j=1}^{m} X_j^= n^$$ $$X_j^, Y_i^\\{0,1\}$$ \(N_i(b_i^B) = \{j \J : P^+ t\,d_{ij} < P^B + t\,d_{,b_i^B}\}\) (capture zone, depends price \(P^\)), \(P^\) = optimized price (returned optimal_price), \(v\) = marginal_cost, \(f_j\) = candidate_fixed_cost, \(n^\) = n_facilities, \(P^B\) = competitor_price, \(t\) = distance_cost_rate. Solved enumerating price breakpoints (see ), directly MINLP.

title: Uncapacitated Fixed-charge Facility Location Problem (UFCLP) — ufclp
text: Chooses candidate sites open, trading site's fixed opening cost transport cost serving demand . Unlike p_median()/mclp(), number open facilities fixed – falls cost tradeoff. $$\text{Minimize } z = \sum_{j=1}^{m} f_j X_j + \alpha \sum_{=1}^{n} \sum_{j=1}^{m} a_i d_{ij} Y_{ij}$$ $$\text{s.t. } \sum_{j=1}^{m} Y_{ij} = 1, \; \forall \qquad Y_{ij} \leq X_j, \; \forall ,j$$ $$X_j \\{0,1\} \qquad Y_{ij} \geq 0$$ \(f_j\) = candidate_fixed_cost, \(\alpha\) = transport_cost_rate, \(a_i\) = demand_weight, \(d_{ij}\) = distance (OD matrix).

title: localalloc 0.2.0
text: Solver engine replaced: dropped ompr/ROI favor building model’s MIP directly sparse matrix (Matrix::sparseMatrix()) solving via Rglpk highs (new default). Large instances took minutes ompr now solve seconds. existing_sites semantics changed mclp()/p_median()/p_center()/ uflp(): forced-open sites now count inside p_facilities budget (p_facilities total number open facilities, just new ones); sf_selected returns every open site source column ("candidate"/"existing"). maxcap()/pmaxcap() unchanged (existing_sites competitor, ). Added plot_sites(): interactive mapview map candidate/demand/ existing sf layers. Package renamed several times since 0.1.0: localalloc -> localocal -> localloc -> localalloc. README rewritten description runnable example ten models.

title: localalloc 0.1.0
text: Initial release. Ten facility-location models: p_median(), p_center(), mclp(), lscp(), ufclp(), cflp(), dp(), uflp(), maxcap(), pmaxcap(). Rewrite original localalloc code base: fixes undefined .build_result() call, missing exports, unused test file; unifies model functions onto one sf/OD input contract. Ships two datasets: small synthetic example (sample_*) real Sherbrooke Bixi bike-share case study (bixi_*) source thesis.
